steps.title: Simple whites
steps.body: Dry Trebbiano suits light, simple food: salads, grilled fish, seafood pasta, fried food and antipasti. Its acidity and neutrality make it refreshing. Lugana, from Turbiana, suits lake fish. Trebbiano d'Abruzzo from top producers suits richer fish and white meat.

steps.title: Vin Santo
steps.body: In Tuscany, Vin Santo is served with cantucci, almond biscuits, dipped into the glass. It also suits blue cheese, nut tarts and dried fruit. Serve at 12 to 14 degrees. It keeps for weeks once opened.

steps.prompt: Which Tuscan biscuits are traditionally dipped in Vin Santo?
steps.explanation: Almond cantucci are the classic match.

steps.body: Serve dry Trebbiano well chilled and young. Its charm is freshness, not complexity.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Dry Trebbiano suits light seafood and antipasti
Vin Santo suits cantucci, blue cheese and nut tarts
Drink dry Trebbiano young; Vin Santo keeps
